Early-stage project · Azerbaijan

Helping shops throw away less food

FreshLoop AI is a tool we are building for supermarkets and food shops. You enter stock, sales and expiry dates; it estimates which products may not sell in time and suggests what to do about them.

The problem

Why shops end up with food they cannot sell

How much customers buy changes with the weather, holidays, the day of the week and prices. If a shop orders too much, food expires and is thrown away. If it orders too little, customers leave without what they came for.

Why Azerbaijan

Fresh products such as dairy, bread, fruit and vegetables have a short shelf life, and demand changes with season and holidays. We think local shops need a tool that fits local products and prices. We tested the prototype with Marjan Market, a store in Baku, to see what real write-offs look like.

The problem

Why shops end up with food they cannot sell

How much customers buy changes with the weather, holidays, the day of the week and prices. If a shop orders too much, food expires and is thrown away. If it orders too little, customers leave without what they came for.

1.05B t

of food was wasted worldwide in 2022, according to UNEP

8–10%

of global greenhouse gas emissions are linked to food loss and waste (UNEP)

For a shop, every product that is thrown away is money already spent. We want to help shops spot that early. UNEP estimates that retail shops accounted for about 131 million tonnes of the 2022 total.

The solution

How the idea works

For each product, the demo compares how much is on the shelf with how much will probably sell before it expires. If there is a surplus, it suggests the first action that makes sense, in this order:

1. Better ordering

Order closer to what will sell so surplus never arrives.

2. Timed markdowns

Lower the price while the product still has shelf life.

3. Redistribution

Give safe surplus food to a partner organisation.

4. Recycling

Send unavoidable waste to permitted processing, not landfill.

Safety comes before savings. FreshLoop never extends a use-by date and never decides alone whether food is safe to sell or donate. Authorised staff approve every action.
About the AI in the name. The demo uses simple formulas, not a trained AI model. We want to build a trained model once we have real sales data.

How the estimates work. All figures on this page are sample estimates from simple rules. Open the box below to see every formula and assumption.

How each number is calculated
  1. Expected sales = average daily sales × days left.
  2. Surplus = stock − expected sales (never below zero). Waste risk = surplus ÷ stock.
  3. Potential loss = surplus × unit cost. This is money already spent on units that may not sell.
  4. Markdown price = normal price × (1 − discount).
  5. Extra units sold = surplus × assumed sell-through (60%).
  6. Revenue from extra units = extra units sold × markdown price.
  7. Margin given away = daily sales × markdown days (up to 2) × price × discount. Regular customers also pay less during a markdown.
  8. Estimated net gain (this period) = revenue from extra units − margin given away. The unit cost is already spent, so it is not subtracted again; it only shows whether the markdown price is below cost.
  9. Still unsold after action = surplus − extra units sold. These units are valued at unit cost as the remaining loss.
  10. Future ordering savings = units you would order less next time × unit cost. It is shown separately and never added to the net gain, so the same unit is not counted twice.

Assumptions

  • Daily sales stay constant and stock is not refilled.
  • A markdown sells about 60% of the surplus and lasts at most the last 2 days.
  • If a product has more than 2 days left, the markdown is planned for its last 2 days, not for today.
  • Zero days left means the product is on its last day. A negative number of days means it has expired and must not be sold.
  • Expected sales can never be negative, and a product with no stock produces no estimate.
  • Every regular buyer during the markdown days gets the lower price.
  • Stock on its last day, or a markdown that would lose money, goes to a staff decision: redistribute if approved, otherwise recycle. No money is counted for it.
  • These are estimates from simple rules, not measured results and not a trained AI model.

The team

About FreshLoop

FreshLoop AI is a student-led project by three team members. We are working on ways to help food shops in Azerbaijan throw away less food. We work on the project together.

Haji Farah

Measuring results

Set up how results are measured: food waste, gross margin after markdowns and on-shelf availability, tracked together, so cutting waste by ordering too little does not count as success. Analyzed inventory data and checked the system's recommendations against the project's performance measures.

Safarli Khadija

Research question

Proposed the central question of the project: can food waste be reduced while keeping profitability and product availability? The question reflects the conditions under which store employees make decisions every day, and it became the foundation of our collaboration with Marjan Market.

Nuriyeva Aydan

Safety and users

Made sure the system respects the people who use it: decisions about food suitability stay with authorized staff, and the tool never extends expiry dates or replaces food safety checks. It supports inventory planning rather than replacing established procedures or employees' professional judgment.

These descriptions are our own summary of what each of us did.

Why Azerbaijan

Fresh products such as dairy, bread, fruit and vegetables have a short shelf life, and demand changes with season and holidays. We think local shops need a tool that fits local products and prices. We tested the prototype with Marjan Market, a store in Baku, to see what real write-offs look like.

What Marjan Market wrote about our work

According to the letter, our work involved:

  • Analyzing inventory data
  • Developing forecasting methods
  • Evaluating potential improvements to inventory planning, and the system's recommendations against performance metrics
  • Considering food waste, gross margins after markdowns and on-shelf availability together
  • Designing the system to support inventory planning rather than replace employees' professional judgment or food safety procedures

“The students contributed to inventory data analysis, forecasting methodology development, and the evaluation of the system's recommendations against performance metrics.”

“FRESHLOOP AI was designed to support inventory planning rather than replace employees' professional judgment or established food safety procedures.”

Abbaszada Vagif, Head of Store Operations, Marjan Market. From the signed letter on the Impact page.

The letter describes the three of us together. It does not list separate tasks for each person.
